title: Managed Inference Assurance Rundown and Evidence Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This document is a compact, contract-friendly attestation template and evidence checklist designed for third-party providers or partners who host or manage inference workloads (including model hosting, maintained model weights, inference endpoints, and telemetry capture) on behalf of Redwood Inference customers. It is intended to be attached as a short addendum to vendor contracts (or used as a questionnaire during onboarding) to accelerate technical assurance review while preserving flexibility for partner-specific architectures.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to managed inference providers, hosted-model partners, and channel partners running customer models or customer data through hosted inference endpoints.
- Covers controls relevant to data confidentiality, model integrity, key management, tenancy isolation, access logging, incident response evidence, and minimal operational observability.
- Not a replacement for a full security assessment or SOC report. Where a SOC2 or equivalent exists, use this checklist to fill gaps specific to inference (KV cache isolation, model weight handling, prompt logging).

High-level attestation statements (sample language to include in contract addendum):
1) Data handling and minimization: Provider attests that all customer inputs, prompts, and generated outputs are processed only for the purpose of providing inference services to the customer and are retained only as expressly permitted by the customer contract. Provider will not use customer prompts/outputs to train or improve models without explicit, written consent.
2) Model custody and integrity: Provider attests that model weights used for customer workloads are either: (a) customer-supplied and stored in a customer-segregated artifact store; or (b) provider-supplied but versioned and immutable for the duration of the contracted rollout. Any model weight updates are recorded with cryptographic checksums and rollout metadata.
3) Key management and secrets: Provider uses customer-managed keys when requested (KMS/HSM) or documents cryptographic key handling for provider-managed keys, including rotation cadence and access controls. Provider attests that secrets and credentials for customer endpoints are never stored in plaintext in logs or telemetry.
4) Network and tenancy isolation: Provider attests to network segmentation controls for customer workloads (VPCs, private subnets, peering rules) and to multi-tenant isolation measures for shared compute (container boundaries, cgroup/namespace segregation, VM tenancy).
5) Access controls and least privilege: Provider maintains RBAC and just-in-time controls for access to production inference environments and audit logs every privileged action.
6) Logging, telemetry, and retention: Provider documents what request/response logging is captured, where it is stored, retention periods, and how to disable or redact PII on a per-customer basis.
7) Incident response and evidence: Provider will notify Redwood (or customer) within contractual SLA timelines for incidents and provide forensic artifacts (logs, timeline, indicators) as part of the technical evidence package.

Minimal evidence checklist (deliverables to attach or provide on request):
- Architecture diagram (one-page) showing data flows for inference requests, model stores, KV/prefix caches, and telemetry sinks.
- Short written control narrative (1–2 pages) for each attestation above.
- List of model artifacts with version IDs and checksums (or description of storage partitioning if provider-managed).
- KMS/HSM configuration summary (who can decrypt, rotation schedule, policies).
- Access control roster snapshot (privileged accounts with recent access dates) and RBAC role descriptions.
- Example sanitized request/response log entries plus the log schema and encryption at rest statement.
- Recent vulnerability/patch cadence summary for inference runtime images/kernels (date of last patch).
- Evidence of backup/restore and retention policy for model artifacts and logs.
- Incident response playbook excerpt showing escalation path and SLA commitments.

Acceptance criteria (how Redwood security will accept the package):
- Architecture diagram and control narratives present no obvious cross-customer data paths and demonstrate separation between control plane and data plane.
- KMS summary shows keys are either customer-managed or provider-managed with enterprise-grade protections and documented rotation.
- Model artifacts list or storage partitioning demonstrates ability to pin or freeze models for given customer workloads.
- Access roster and logging examples show auditability and no plaintext secrets in logs.
- If any checklist items are missing, provider must supply a remediation plan and timelines; critical gaps (unencrypted logs, shared mutable model weights without checksum/version control) block onboarding.

Suggested timelines for evidence delivery (negotiable per contract size):
- Initial evidence bundle: within 10 business days of contract signature or SOW acceptance.
- Full technical walk-through and access to sanitized logs: within 20 business days.
- Remediation plan for any gaps: initial remediation proposal within 5 business days of gap identification; target remediation completion dates tied to risk severity.

Risk flags (examples that require additional review or contractual controls):
- Provider uses customer data to continuously train or fine-tune shared models without explicit agreement.
- Model weights are stored in a single shared bucket with no per-customer partitioning or access controls.
- Request/response logs are stored unencrypted for more than 30 days by default and cannot be redacted.
- No documented key rotation or keys accessible to more than a small admin group without JIT controls.

Contract clauses to consider (examples):
- Model Non-Use Clause: provider shall not use customer prompts or outputs to improve, fine-tune, or benchmark provider models absent explicit written consent.
- Evidence Production Clause: provider shall produce the listed evidence within specified timelines and designate a technical contact for follow-up.
- Escrow/Sequester Right: on termination or upon agreed triggers, customer may require model artifacts and logs to be sequestered and delivered to a specified archive location.
- Subprocessor/Subcontractor Disclosure: provider shall list subprocessors relevant to inference (hosting, telemetry, storage) and update the list within 10 days of changes.

Quick onboarding checklist (for internal use):
1) Send initial evidence template to provider (this doc + list).
2) Triage returned evidence: Architecture, KMS, models, logs, access controls.
3) Mark any critical gaps and generate SEC-xxxxx Jira ticket and remediation plan.
4) Schedule a technical walkthrough with provider infra/security + Redwood SRE and product owner.
5) Accept or escalate to legal for contract-specific clauses.

Notes and discussion items (open/draft):
- How strict should the Model Non-Use Clause be for upstream open models that the provider also serves to other customers? We should allow providers to host open models but prevent customer prompt reuse.
- Decide on a default max retention for request/response logs for managed inference (30 days recommended, with opt-in longer retention for customers).
- Consider a lightweight cryptographic fingerprint requirement for model weights (sha256) to ensure traceability during rollouts.

Appendix A — One-paragraph attestation template (copy/paste for vendor addendum):
"Provider attests, under penalty of contractual remedy, that during the term of this agreement: (i) customer inputs and generated outputs are processed only to provide inference services and are not used to train provider models unless the parties agree in writing; (ii) model artifacts serving customer workloads are versioned and immutable for the duration of the deployment and are accompanied by checksums; (iii) cryptographic keys used to protect customer data are managed as described in the attached KMS summary; and (iv) access to production inference environments is logged and auditable. Provider shall furnish the evidence bundle listed in the attached checklist within the timelines specified.

Signature:
Provider security lead: ______________________   Date: __________
Redwood reviewer: __________________________  Date: __________

END OF DOCUMENT"
